title: Soul Vacuum
paragraphs: “But that’s only if no mysterious factors were involved. However, the fact that the legend was successfully preserved…”
“Yes. It’s likely that the Four Holy Heroes or the Seven Star Heroes were summoned in time and managed to stop it beforehand.”
“So, that means the heroes didn’t just fall prey to the enemy’s attacks, huh?”
“Going back to the topic, Pope, do you know how they defeated such enemies?”

“Um… I believe there are a few records. Joining forces with the possessed and saving them miraculously with the power of the weapon… defeating them by borrowing the power of monsters… I think it was something along those lines. Yes.”
“The first one sounds like something we’ve already done, right? With the King of Melromarc.”
“Ah… true, though the order was a bit different, it was essentially the same.”
“The power of the weapon, huh…”
“Even weapons that were supposed to be effective against ghosts didn’t work that well, right?”
“I believe Motoyasu’s Soul Eater Spear was effective.”
Ren looks at me. I switch my spear to the Soul Eater Spear.
“Should I just stab and kill with this?”
“No, no, that’s not good. It seems to be physically effective.”
Oh? This is becoming troublesome.
“You’re assuming the enemy will show up, but the real challenge is identifying them first.”
“Right. We’re considering the possibility that it’s possession, not body-switching.”
“But if you use that spear skillfully, it might be possible to eliminate only the soul without harming the body.”
“Well, that would be ideal. Like how a body in a brain-dead state can still be used for organ donation.”
“Are you thinking that body-switching stems from that idea?”
“I don’t think so… Hmm…”
It seems to be a difficult problem, and Father continues to groan over it. That knight is quite the difficult case.
“Wouldn’t it be fine to just take down such a lowly pig’s rampage and be done with it?”
“…Motoyasu, wouldn’t you hate it if someone took over your body and made you rampage? Even if you knew the only way to save yourself was to die.”
Indeed, I would hate that. But if I were possessed and caused trouble for Father, it would be far better for me to be taken down.
“Um… but what if it was Sakura-chan and the others who were possessed? What would you do, Motoyasu?”
What?! Such a thing! There’s no way I could harm Sakura-chan and the others!
“Ugh… this is an extremely difficult problem!”
“His eyes have changed…”
“Lately, I feel like I’m starting to figure out how to control Motoyasu…”
“W-Well, I was thinking the same thing after hearing about when I rampaged with the Cursed Shield…”
So that’s how it was. Either way, we need to come up with a concrete solution.
“And then… borrowing the power of monsters, huh?”
“You asked Gaelion about that, didn’t you?”
“Gaelion-chan may be the king of monsters, but he’s not an expert, right? There’s… oh yeah, wasn’t there a monster called Soul Vacuumer living in the king’s harem?”
“Ah, now that you mention it. A monster that devours souls.”
“The Soul Eater is apparently a monster that came from the waves, but the Vacuumer is a monster native to this world.”
“Then… shouldn’t we just bring Gaelion along and have him translate? Assuming it can even communicate, that is.”
“Also… speaking of monsters, we should consult Rat-san as well. Pope, thank you for your advice.”
“Not at all. All is in the name of the Four Holy Heroes, who are our gods… I am glad if I could be of any help. Yes.”
The pope is praying. For now, we headed to the building that the physician had newly taken as a temporary base.
“So, you came to me.”
“That’s right.”
“Well, it’s certainly an interesting story.”

The physician, as usual, seems to have set up a research lab and is continuing her studies. Moreover, thanks to her record of conducting examinations on our Filolials and Gaelion, she’s been given some degree of special treatment.
“Research on monsters that are said to feed on souls hasn’t progressed much. Given their nature, even humans with high potential can be greatly affected… and it’s a field that’s considered taboo.”
“Well, that’s understandable…”
One wrong step in how they’re used, and it could lead to disaster. That’s probably why even Faubrey handled this matter with some caution.
“But at the same time, we can’t completely ignore them since they’re effective against ghost-type monsters.”
“They seem effective against undead, after all.”
“Right. Ghosts that even ordinary adventurers can see are probably only found in notorious places like ancient battlefields.”
“So they do exist, huh?”
What’s with that surprise now?
“The most famous example… would be the underground space of the magic city, where, due to the concentration of magical energy, an almost infinite number of them exist—”
“Ah, I know about that city from the game.”
“Oh? Is that so?”
Itsuki has stopped. In my case, it was the underground prison. When I asked Ren later, he said it was a huge tower.

That place has terrible experience points. The drops are so-so, but overall, it’s worse than the Spirit Tortoise, making it an unpopular map. It used to boast magic, but now it’s a disappointing country that loses out to both Faubrey and Zeltoble.
Well, at best, the mountains with plenty of Airwake Ore make for a decent tourist attraction. If you fly there by plane, you’ll crash immediately.
“So, the question is whether the soul inside the body is the original person or someone else, right?”
“I guess that’s what it comes down to?”

“Maybe I should submit this for the next contest? I’ve been cautious because I didn’t know how people would react, but if it’s something consulted on by the Four Holy Heroes, there shouldn’t be any complaints.”
“Would that win you an award?”
“Oh? Don’t the Four Holy Heroes know? Lately, nobles from various countries have been growing suspicious of their own sons and daughters.”
Ah… Father nodded weakly with an apologetic look. What does that mean?
“Well, when the one who killed the Seven Star Hero turned out to be a young noble, and there are others like him, wouldn’t they wonder if their own sons might be the same…?”
“Exactly. And then there’s the sudden development of new technology or unusually strong combat skills, all kinds of factors.”
“The more someone stands out, the more their family starts to suspect them. It’s unbearable for the innocent ones.”
“Because of that, there’s talk about whether the judgment of the Four Holy Heroes was truly just.”
“We hadn’t heard anything about that.”
“Eclair might have known.”
“Eclair is training at the castle, right? She mentioned having passionate discussions with Rollick and the others about chivalry.”
“What about Éclair?”
At my question, Father and the others snapped back to reality.
“We definitely caught the culprit, and it’s true that many of the challengers were the children of nobles… but that was also the enemy’s objective. It’s not like it was our fault…”
“I know. That’s why if we create something that resolves those concerns, we could make a fortune and aim for anything.”

The physician is deep in thought. …Wasn’t an alchemist’s job to create such things? From what I remember from the game, their job was to make herbs or maybe some kind of combat pet. They were considered the weakest class after shield users. Reality is different from games, after all.
“So, what if there was a tool that could instantly distinguish reincarnators?”
Father and the others clapped their hands.
“Ah, that would be a very useful invention.”
“If that tool could also identify possessed individuals, it would be incredibly helpful.”
“If it could be done, that is.”
“That’s the tricky part…”
The physician is scribbling notes on paper with her pen.

“Like I mentioned earlier, research on monsters that are said to feed on souls hasn’t progressed much. It’s considered taboo. At best, the church performs exorcisms and spirit banishments, and only uses them to subjugate truly stubborn evil spirits.”
“Given their nature, raising them must be quite difficult.”
“That depends on the type. A Soul Vacuumer, for example, is something even an ordinary person could defeat.”
“They’re that weak?”
“Legends and fairy tales make them seem scary, but they’re just distant relatives of Dune and are quite docile by nature.”
“What’s so scary about them?” Ren asks the physician.
Indeed, Dune isn’t scary at all. I remember Father’s village even kept them.

“The version of the Soul Vacuumer told to children goes like this: ‘If you’re bad, the Soul Vacuumer will come at night and suck out your soul.’ It’s a common phrase parents use to discipline their kids. But in reality, they can’t take souls from living people.”
